content:
I found a feature hidden in the System Settings app today that I didn't know existed: you can set a default language for individual Mac apps. If you already knew this, there's nothing to see here, move along. But if you didn't, here's how it works (and what it can't do)…

In reality, there are many bilingual people who need to switch languages throughout the day depending on who they're talking to or what they're working on. I don't have that problem, but I do often need to switch between British English (or English…) and American English.

(To be clear, that was a joke earlier! English has some usages that have been preserved in American English but later changed in British English, such as the word ending -ize becoming -ise in the UK. Also, as James Nicoll put it: "The problem with defending the purity of the English language is that English is a mess to begin with. It's not just borrowing words willy-nilly; sometimes it stalks other languages down dark alleys and beats them unconscious and rifles through their pockets for new vocabulary.")

Switching between the two means I can't rely entirely on spell check to catch the cases where I've used the right word but the wrong version. I always thought this was something I just had to handle manually, but today I found at least one and a half solutions.

At the bottom of System Preferences > General > Language & Region, there's a hidden "Applications" tab. You can add apps to it and select a language. Apple's American-centric thinking shines through here: British English is called "English (UK)" and American English is called "English – English."

In my case, most of my writing happens in the browser, so I use two different browsers depending on the target language. I have British English set as the system language, so Safari uses British English; Chrome (which appears in the list alphabetically as Google Chrome) is set to American English.

However, I found one very important limitation: only apps that support the macOS localisation/language API can be set this way, so not all apps will appear in the list.

If I'm the last person in the world to find this out, feel free to laugh at me in the comments with your multilingual superiority.
